text: BROKE / BILLIONAIRE / 50M USERS / $2B [props: laptop bubble "your app save me"; paper stack labelled "feedback"]
scene: Hard vertical split. Left panel: a glasses-wearing, brown-haired cartoon character typing at a lamp-lit laptop in a dark room, one tear on his cheek, a feedback paper stack at his elbow. Right panel: the same character, arms crossed and heavy-lidded, standing in a glass-walled office before a wall screen showing 50M USERS, $2B and a rising green arrow, with desk silhouettes behind him.
mechanism: Same-character transformation told by a split frame: the BROKE/BILLIONAIRE word pair and the rising chart deliver the whole arc at once, while the flat stare on the right hints at the title's "evil" turn.
composition: Primary focal points are the two headline words across the top of each half; secondary is the lamp-lit face on the left and the standing figure on the right. The centre seam divides the frame roughly 50/50, figures fill about two thirds of the height, and the green chart line on the right gives an up-and-right diagonal.
typography: Two single-word headlines in condensed heavy sans, red on near-black and pale yellow on grey-teal; both survive at 160x90. The chart labels 50M USERS and $2B are mid-size; axis digits are noise. The title adds POV and evil framing that the thumbnail text lacks.
colors: Amber lamp glow against near-black navy on the left; desaturated teal-grey with cyan screen glow on the right. Red BROKE is the only warm alert hue and yellow BILLIONAIRE marks the success side, so colour tracks the narrative. Contrast between panels is strong, inside the right office it is weaker.
psychology: Left character shows a tear and slumped shoulders (vulnerability, sympathy); right character is heavy-lidded with crossed arms, readable as cold or smug, consistent with the villain framing in the title but not shown as explicit villainy.
partnership: Title promises a startup-to-evil-billionaire arc; the thumbnail supplies both endpoints and the numbers but nothing explicitly evil beyond the stony stare, so the open question is what turns him. Reveal risk is low because the middle of the story is absent.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red BROKE first, eye hops over the seam to BILLIONAIRE, then drops to the glowing chart numbers and finally to the tear-streaked face by the lamp.
art: Flat 2D cartoon with soft gradient lighting; lamp glow and screen glow are coherent. Tiny axis strings beside the wall screen read like pseudo-numbers that do not resolve into legible values, a minor text artefact visible only at native size. Background is moderately busy with desk silhouettes.
strength: Clean before/after split with only two headline words keeps the transformation readable even at 160x90.
weakness: The payoff panel is the weaker half: grey office, small unexpressive figure and desk silhouettes dilute the success image.
bottleneck: The payoff panel has no visible "evil" cue, so the title's most distinctive word has no visual support.
action: Hypothesis: add one villain cue to the right panel (a smirk plus red backlight on the screen) and compare it against the current neutral stare.
counterexample: Seq 22 (THB-e88a25a1a97b) has no headline text and no comparison structure, so it does the opposite by leaning on one scene alone.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: Dies Every Week [thin handwritten black script, two lines, right of creature]
scene: A mud-brown, wrinkled, bear-like creature (the tardigrade of the title is not named on the image) crouches on cracked dry ground, mouth wide open in a scream with a ring of small teeth visible, red-rimmed eyes, tears and saliva dripping, short claws splayed. A hand-drawn curved arrow runs from the handwritten text toward its head. White background with dirt speckles at lower left.
mechanism: Pity-and-shock: a visibly anguished creature plus a stark mortality statement ("Dies Every Week") makes the title's parenthetical concrete and slightly absurd.
composition: Creature occupies the left 55% with a low, centred-left mass; text sits right in two lines with a curved arrow bridging them. The native file is a 480x360 frame with black bars above and below, so the real art is a letterboxed band; ample white negative space on the right.
typography: Three words in thin handwritten black script, split over two lines ("Dies Every" / "Week"); roughly 15% of frame height per line. Stroke weight is light, so at 160x90 the words soften. It repeats the title's parenthetical and adds no new information.
colors: Earth browns and tan against pure white give strong figure/ground separation; the only accents are red eye rims and pale blue tears. No warning colour is used and the palette is otherwise muted.
psychology: Open-mouthed scream, streaming tears and drooping posture read as suffering and helplessness, inviting sympathy and a grim-humour reaction; no authority or credential cues are present.
partnership: Title says it sucks to be born a tardigrade and that it dies every week; the thumbnail duplicates the "dies every week" half and supplies the emotional image, but never names the animal, so the species lives only in the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the wailing mouth and eyes catch first, the arrow then pulls the eye to "Dies Every Week" on the right.
art: Painterly ink-and-wash texture with plausible shading on the wrinkled body; speckled dirt and cracked ground are coherent. Letterbox bars and the low 480x360 native resolution cost sharpness, which is a capture limit rather than a design choice.
strength: A single memorable expression on a single creature, with the curved arrow handing the eye to a short mortality phrase.
weakness: Thin handwritten lettering is the lightest element on the page, so the key phrase is weaker than the creature and may be lost on small screens.
bottleneck: The thin script is not heavy enough to carry the "dies every week" hook at phone size.
action: Hypothesis: set "Dies Every Week" in a heavier hand-lettered weight with a dark outline and test legibility at 160x90 against the thin version.
counterexample: Seq 8 (THB-80d04296c973) uses the same sad-animal formula but with a very heavy "GONE" word, showing the stronger text treatment.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: DRUNK ALL DAY? [yellow outlined caps, full top edge]
scene: A shaggy-haired caveman figure with a white round face, bloodshot droopy eyes, flushed cheeks and a drooling grin gives a thumbs-up with one hand and holds a lumpy clay cup of red-brown liquid in the other. Behind him a cave mouth frames a smiling cartoon sun; broken pottery shards and a bone litter the floor.
mechanism: Absurd-comedy: a visibly intoxicated caveman with a thumbs-up turns the title's dry history question into a joke the viewer wants explained.
composition: The big face on the right and the cup on the left form the two focal points with the thumbs-up as a tertiary beat; the smiling sun sits between them in the cave opening. Headline spans the full width at the top, the figure is cropped by the lower edge, with mild clutter from shards and rocks.
typography: Three words, all caps, thick yellow letters with a black outline spanning the full top edge; they are the largest element and stay readable at 160x90. The question mark creates uncertainty; the title's "ancient humans" and "first" are not on the image.
colors: Warm muddy browns and greys form the background while saturated yellow headline, pink cheeks and white face pop out. The yellow-black text pairing carries the highest contrast; no warning red is used.
psychology: Glassy half-closed eyes, flushed cheeks, drool and a thumbs-up read as cheerful drunkenness, an inviting rather than threatening tone; no authority cues.
partnership: Title asks when ancient humans first drank alcohol; the thumbnail swaps the scholarly question for a "were they always drunk?" joke, escalating the entertainment angle while leaving the actual answer (when) open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow DRUNK ALL DAY? line is read first, then the red-eyed face, then the cup and thumbs-up.
art: Clean vector cartoon with consistent outlines; the cup, face and sun are well separated by value. Background is moderate but desaturated so it does not compete. Survives 160x90 well.
strength: A single comic expression (red eyes, drool, thumbs-up) delivers the premise instantly and is visible at phone size.
weakness: The thumbnail frames ancient people as perpetual drunks, which may promise a gag the history video does not center on.
bottleneck: Promise drift risk: "DRUNK ALL DAY?" is a funnier claim than the neutral "first drink" title.
action: Hypothesis: add a small "10,000 years ago" or equivalent date tag to anchor the joke in the title's historical question and test against the current version.
counterexample: Seq 10 (THB-b36d76106c1c) is a serious, text-restrained history thumbnail with no comic face, the opposite tonal choice.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: AUG 31, 2010 [tiny caption left of the diver]
scene: SHORTS vertical artwork: a pale grey centre strip (about a third of the frame width) flanked by darker grey blurred side bars. mechanism: Minimalist xkcd-style deadpan: a lone diver with a bucket is an intrigue-by-oddity image, but no nuclear element is shown so the hook rests on the title.
composition: The diver is a tiny mark floating in the upper-middle of the strip; most of the strip is empty grey. The date caption is offset to the left of the figure, and there is no focal hierarchy beyond the figure itself.
typography: Three small words and numerals in a thin handwritten-style caption (about 3% of frame height); invisible at 160x90. It adds a date not mentioned in the title and no connection to the question asked.
colors: Near-monochrome: pale grey strip, mid-grey bars, black line art, white bubbles. Mean saturation is effectively zero; no accent hue and no warning colour exist.
psychology: Neutral, whimsical and calm; there is no face, gaze or emotional signal, and nothing communicates danger or authority.
partnership: Title asks whether you could swim in a spent nuclear fuel pool; the diver gear loosely answers "swim" but nothing shows nuclear fuel or the answer, leaving the whole question for the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: eye lands on the black diver silhouette, then flicks to the date caption; the grey bars are skipped.
art: Hand-drawn thin-line stick art on a flat grey fill with blurred side extension; very simple and coherent. Scale is the main issue: the figure occupies under 5% of the frame area.
strength: The line-art diver with a bucket is quirky and consistent with a distinct hand-drawn channel look.
weakness: The figure is tiny and low-contrast in a mostly empty grey strip, with side bars adding no information.
bottleneck: At feed size the diver and caption are almost invisible, so nothing communicates the nuclear premise.

text: FIRST WHITE? [yellow outlined caps, full top edge]
scene: Five cartoon figures stand in a line on a green field under a grey sky, drawn with stick limbs and large round heads and wide eyes. Skin tones run from very dark on the left through brown and tan to a pure white face on the right; clothing runs from thick fur and a tooth necklace to a feathered headband to grass skirts and a single torn hide on the white figure. All five stare with deadpan sideways eyes.
mechanism: A skin-tone gradient line-up makes "who is the first white one?" a visual puzzle; the thumbnail relies on a sensitive identity comparison to trigger curiosity.
composition: Strong horizontal row with the five heads evenly spaced across the middle band, a headline band at the top, and the white figure at the far right as the culminating focal point. Little negative space and uniform scale; symmetric rather than dynamic.
typography: Two words in thick yellow outlined caps across the full top; the largest element and fully legible at 160x90. It repeats the title's core question in shorter form, with the question mark as the only added signal.
colors: Saturated yellow headline over a bright green field and grey sky; skin-tone gradient from dark brown to white is the semantic device. Earth-tone clothing keeps figures unified; no warning colour.
psychology: Identical deadpan sideways glances create an awkward, comedic tension; the lone white figure, wide-eyed and last in line, signals bewilderment rather than authority.
partnership: Title asks why ancient humans became white; thumbnail compresses this to "FIRST WHITE?" and shows a visual lineup, answering nothing but turning an evolutionary question into an identity-sorting game, which may hint at a framing more provocative than explanatory.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow FIRST WHITE? is read, then the eye sweeps along the row left to right and rests on the white figure at the end.
art: Flat cartoon with consistent outlines, cohesive costume details (bones in hair, cowrie beads, feather headband) and neat alignment. At 160x90 the five figures merge into a uniform band but the dark-to-white progression remains visible.
strength: The dark-to-white gradient lineup is instantly graspable at 160x90 and sets up a clear visual question.
weakness: The figures have identical expressions and poses, so beyond skin tone and clothing they carry little emotional variety.
bottleneck: Heavily reliant on a sensitive racial-identity comparison; the distinctiveness is the contrast itself, with little added story.
action: Hypothesis: replace "FIRST WHITE?" with a more neutral hook such as "WHY SKIN COLOUR CHANGED?" and A/B whether the lineup still lands without the identity framing.
counterexample: Seq 13 (THB-64e7d765abaf) puts one calm figure against multiple animals, building contrast through reaction rather than a spectrum of identities.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: "NO." / $1.84 Billion [check header text garbled: "ACQUISITION DOEK", "300$"]
scene: A smooth-faced cartoon character in a navy cap and grey t-shirt, smirking, holds a flat palm toward two older suited men in a high-rise boardroom at golden hour; one man grips an oversized cheque labelled $1.84 Billion and looks alarmed, the other stares wide-eyed. Skyline with a pointed tower fills the windows; a red curved arrow runs from the quoted "NO." to the cap character.
mechanism: Refusal-of-a-fortune scene: a casual young figure rejecting a huge cheque in front of shocked executives dramatises the title's "built in silence" achievement as a single defiant gesture.
composition: Left-heavy: the large cap character with the stop hand at left, the cheque as the secondary focal point on the right, with a diagonal from the red arrow into the face. Table edge and cups form a foreground band; the skyline backdrop makes the frame busy.
typography: Quoted white "NO." in heavy caps with a dark edge at top-centre is large and survives; the "$1.84 Billion" on the cheque is small and thin-weight, lost at 160x90. The quotes frame the word as speech.
colors: Golden-orange sunset glow with deep brown wood and navy suits; the white NO. and red arrow cut through the warm field. Saturation is high and the palette cohesive; red used only for the arrow.
psychology: Confident smile with a raised stop palm contrasts with the two executives' alarmed brows and open eyes: status reversal, defiance and shock cues.
partnership: Title is a POV about building $1.8 Billion in silence as a first-generation founder; the thumbnail turns the figure into a $1.84 Billion cheque refusal, adding a dramatic moment that the title does not state and risking promise drift if the video is about quiet building.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white "NO." in quotes first, the red arrow carries the eye to the smug cap character, then to the raised hand and the two shocked executives with the cheque.
art: Polished cartoon render with warm sun glow and consistent perspective across the table and windows. The cheque header and bank-number lines are garbled glyphs ("ACQUISITION DOEK", "300$"), an AI-style text artefact visible at native size only. High background complexity from the skyline.
strength: Strong status-reversal narrative in one frame: casual figure refuses a billion-dollar cheque while executives react.
weakness: The cheque amount is small and thin, and the busy skyline plus warm orange fill compete with the NO.
bottleneck: The dollar figure that makes the refusal meaningful is illegible at feed size.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the cheque to roughly twice its current size and set "$1.84B" in bold white-on-green, then compare recall of the amount at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 17 (THB-7b3efc3ca277) keeps a white background and a bold headline; the opposite of this crowded, golden-hour scene.

text: Almost / GONE [thin handwritten "Almost" above heavy "GONE"]
scene: A chubby grey porpoise-like animal (the vaquita of the title is not named) hangs tangled in a knotted fishing net at the water line, eyes bloodshot and wide, tears streaming, sweat drops, mouth open in a wail, flippers raised and motion marks around it. A hand-drawn black arrow curves from the text to its flipper-body. White background with a splash of blue water at the bottom.
mechanism: Pathos-led scarcity: a visibly terrified animal caught in a net plus the word GONE turns an endangered-species fact into an emotional rescue question.
composition: The animal fills the left two thirds, the net crosses the whole lower-left, and the right third holds two stacked words with a curved arrow into the creature. Face is near the centre of the subject, there is clear white negative space beside the text, and the diagonal net lines lead to the face.
typography: "Almost" in thin handwritten black over a much larger heavy "GONE"; the size jump makes GONE the dominant word and both stay legible at 160x90. The title gives the species and "sucks to be born"; the thumbnail adds the extinction stakes.
colors: Cool slate greys and blue water on pure white, with pink mouth and red-rimmed eyes as the only warm accents; the black text and net lines separate cleanly from the background. No warning colour used.
psychology: Frightened wide eyes, flowing tears and a wailing mouth communicate distress and urgency; the mortality word GONE adds loss and fear, inviting sympathy rather than authority cues.
partnership: Title says it sucks to be born as a vaquita; the thumbnail adds the near-extinction stakes ("Almost GONE") and a visible cause (a net), a strong complement that raises the question of how few remain.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the huge black GONE and the crying face compete first, the arrow loops from the word onto the netted body, and the net pattern ends the scan at lower left.
art: Clean, high-detail vector cartoon with consistent shading on the animal, tear highlights and rope knots. The expression is exaggerated but coherent; the white background keeps it uncluttered and it holds up at 160x90.
strength: A heavy single word plus a distressed, well-lit character gives a very clear, emotionally loaded read at phone size.
weakness: The net crosses the whole body, giving the lower-left some visual busyness, and the thin "Almost" is the weakest element.
bottleneck: The creature is never named, so the species identification relies on the title.
action: Hypothesis: thicken "Almost" to match the weight of "GONE" and test whether the pair reads as a single phrase at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 2 (THB-c58352f4aa17) uses the same crying-animal device but with thin script and a letterboxed frame, which weakens the text.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: YOUR LIFE / EVERY FBI SINPER RANK [helmet and vest: FBI, FBI HRT; shoulder patch: SNIPER]
scene: A cartoon operator with a round white face, angry V-shaped brows and a pursed mouth stands at the left in a green camouflage kit: helmet with FBI lettering, night-vision goggles flipped up, headset microphone, a vest marked FBI HRT, a SNIPER shoulder patch, and a long camo-taped scoped rifle with bipod pointing right across the lower frame. Plain white background.
mechanism: Role-immersion POV: a heavily kitted FBI sniper cartoon and a bold "YOUR LIFE" label cast the viewer as the person climbing the ranks.
composition: The figure fills the left 55% with the rifle sweeping diagonally to the right edge; the red-boxed headline and the second line stack in the upper right. Face sits at upper-left near a third; strong diagonal from helmet to muzzle, generous white space around the text.
typography: White "YOUR LIFE" in huge condensed caps on a red box, then "EVERY FBI SINPER RANK" in black caps with a shadow. "SINPER" is visibly misspelled (the shoulder patch spells SNIPER correctly). The second line is smaller and thin at 160x90; the headline survives.
colors: Olive and tan camouflage against a pure white background, with a single saturated red-box headline as the alert accent; red is used as a label, not a danger signal. Subject separation is strong; overall palette is cohesive.
psychology: Scowling brows and a rigid stance signal intensity and authority; the weapon adds threat. The scowl is exaggerated cartoon aggression rather than a documentary face.
partnership: Title is a POV about rising through FBI sniper ranks and "The Real Story"; the thumbnail supplies the sniper image and a vague "YOUR LIFE" line that does not say what happens to it, leaving the stakes unspecified; the visible misspelling undercuts the "real story" authority.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red-boxed YOUR LIFE first, then the armed figure's scowl, then the second line, with the rifle muzzle leading out of frame.
art: Detailed vector-cartoon rendering with consistent camo pattern and gear details; the camouflage and rifle are highly detailed relative to the blank face. The word SINPER is a visible spelling error at native size. At 160x90 the camo detail merges into an olive mass.
strength: Detailed gear (FBI HRT vest, night-vision, camo rifle) reads as a specific role and gives the thumbnail a distinctive subject.
weakness: "YOUR LIFE" is vague without a verb, and the second line is both small and misspelled.
bottleneck: The visible "SINPER" typo conflicts with a "real story" claim and attracts attention to error instead of the rank hook.
action: Hypothesis: correct the spelling and replace "YOUR LIFE" with a rank-escalation phrase such as "RANK 1 TO 5" to test whether a concrete progression increases clarity.
counterexample: Seq 20 (THB-45b206bce442) labels its subjects with short callout words (KREMLIN, GERMAN) that are spelled correctly and carry the story.

text: IRAN / 5000 BC – 2026 [black serif caps, right side]
scene: A flat illustrated panorama: a tall rocky plateau topped by a columned palace complex with two bull-headed column tops, a long stone staircase flanked by lion statues rising along its face, and a smaller stepped tower mid-slope. Below spreads a dense desert city with domes, minarets and a brick tower; tiny people dot the stairs and plaza. Pale blue sky fills the right half.
mechanism: Scale-of-time panorama: a monumental ancient-to-modern cityscape with a date span signals a whole-civilisation overview rather than a person-focused story.
composition: The plateau and palace dominate the left 55%, the staircase forming a diagonal into the city; text stacks on the right in empty sky, balancing the heavy left. Subject scale is large, clutter is concentrated in the lower city band, and the text area has clean space.
typography: "IRAN" in large black serif caps above "5000 BC – 2026" in smaller bold serif; two lines, four words, high contrast on pale blue and readable at 160x90. The title's "ENTIRE ... in 11 Minutes" is not on the image.
colors: Sandstone ochres and browns against light sky blue, with small terracotta and green accents in the city; palette is cohesive and low-aggression. Black text on pale blue gives strong text contrast; no warning colour.
psychology: No faces or gestures; the monumental staircase and fortress read as grandeur and antiquity, evoking curiosity or awe rather than urgency, vulnerability or fear.
partnership: Title promises the entire history of Iran in 11 minutes; the thumbnail adds the 5000 BC–2026 span and a monumental image, matching scale but not the "11 minutes" promise or any emotional hook.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the big serif IRAN first, then the date line beneath it, then the eye drifts left up the staircase to the palace.
art: Detailed hand-drawn style with consistent perspective and flat shading; the palace, staircase and lions are coherent. The dense lower city adds visual noise but stays low contrast and does not collide with the text.
strength: Clear, honest scale cue with a precise date range and a recognisable ancient landmark.
weakness: No human figure or emotional event, so the image reads as an encyclopedia plate rather than a hook.
bottleneck: Low emotional tension: the thumbnail promises breadth but offers no question or conflict to resolve.
action: Hypothesis: add one dramatic contrast element (e.g. a split showing an ancient palace against a modern skyline) and compare against the current single-era scene.
counterexample: Seq 3 (THB-7e9cce1c536b) leads with a comic face and a question-mark headline, the opposite emotional strategy to this restrained panorama.

medical_notes: "DEATH STARTS IN YOUR LEGS" plus an "EAT THIS IMMEDIATELY" demand implies a diet can avert death, a claim that needs content evidence the title does not state.
text: DEATH STARTS IN YOUR LEGS / IF YOU ARE OVER 60 / EAT THIS / IMMEDIATELY!
scene: A smiling grey-bearded older man in a teal polo stands at the right, holding a plate with sweet-potato cubes, blueberries, halved boiled eggs, two sardines and a mound of lentils. Black background; the text stacks on the left in four lines with the last word in a red box.
mechanism: Fear-then-remedy: a mortality statement tied to the legs, an age gate and a food plate promise an urgent dietary fix.
composition: Four stacked lines fill the left 60%, the man occupies the right 40% with the plate at lower right as the hero object; the face sits at upper right. The headline-dominated layout leaves little negative space and the man is cropped at the thighs.
typography: Large bold caps in yellow, white and white-on-red across four lines, 13 words; the density is high and the smaller lines compress at 160x90 though the first line and red IMMEDIATELY! remain legible. The title's "6 foods" and "FAST" are partially restated.
colors: Pure black background with yellow, white and red text, plus a teal shirt and colourful plate; red box adds urgency and the black field gives maximum text contrast. Saturation is high with no soft midtones.
psychology: The man's relaxed, pleased smile contradicts the dread of "DEATH STARTS"; the text carries the fear while the face reassures, producing mixed emotional signals. Age appears in text ("OVER 60") rather than in a person-specific cue.
partnership: Title says your legs weaken first and to eat 6 foods; the thumbnail escalates "weaken" to "DEATH STARTS IN YOUR LEGS" and adds an urgency demand, which the title does not state; the plate shows food but not six items.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow DEATH STARTS first, then the white age line, then EAT THIS and the red IMMEDIATELY! box, with the plate and the smiling man read last.
art: Soft illustrated-realistic style with plausible lighting on the man and plate; hands and plate are coherent. Large flat text area dominates the surface, and compressed lower lines reduce readability at phone size.
strength: A very strong, instantly legible fear headline and a concrete plate that signals a food-based remedy.
weakness: Four stacked lines and thirteen words overload the frame, and the cheerful face contradicts the "death" message.
bottleneck: The fear escalation ("DEATH STARTS") goes beyond the title's claim and risks overstating the health stakes.
action: Hypothesis: shorten to two lines ("LEG WEAKNESS AFTER 60 / EAT THESE 6") with a concerned expression and compare readability and tone at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 16 (THB-b1def3ce359a) uses a similar black-and-yellow format with fewer words and a visible scanner, the more restrained version.
hero_object: plate of sardines, eggs, lentils and berries
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

medical_notes: A cure-style claim to "unclog brain vessels" with one spoon a month over a red-vessel image presents an unsupported treatment and no named ingredient or credential.
text: UNCLOG BRAIN VESSELS / ONLY 1 SPOON A MONTH
scene: Split frame under a full-width yellow banner. Left: a translucent grey head profile in teal-blue haze with a tangle of bright red vessels over the brain and down the neck. colors: White ground, black outlines and text, a skin-tone figure and a single green spike as the colour accent; green connotes gains. Low saturation overall and no warning red, so the urgency comes from the text and posture.
psychology: The wide-eyed, mouth-open shout reads as excitement or alarm; the vertical spike and "ARE YOU READY" add urgency and fear-of-missing-out.
partnership: Title says the SpaceX IPO is about to flip your 401k and most people are not ready; the thumbnail turns it into a flat-versus-spike chart and a readiness question, complementing the title but implying a gain the content may not support.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the huge face and ARE YOU READY?! first, then the black arrow drives the eye to the green spike, with SPACEX and 401K labels last.
art: Clean thick-outline cartoon with the grid drawn in perspective; the chart is simple and consistent. The line chart is schematic with no axis values, so it is a symbol rather than data.
strength: A clear flat-versus-spike chart with two labels turns a news event into a simple visual in one glance.
weakness: The chart has no scale or evidence, so the implied "spike" is only an illustration.
bottleneck: The excited face and spike imply a gain, while the title implies risk, so the emotional direction is ambiguous.
action: Hypothesis: label the spike with a concrete figure (e.g. "+40%?") and compare a worried face vs the current excited face for direction of emotion.
counterexample: Seq 24 (THB-ac304279eb61) shows the opposite: a real photo with tiny text and no chart or graphic cue.

text: GOOD BALANCE ✅ / STRONG LEGS 🦶
scene: SHORTS vertical frame: a centre photo strip of a smiling older man with short grey hair and a grey polo, a bag strap across his chest, in front of blurred green trees, flanked by blurred green side bars. mechanism: Outcome label on a stock-style portrait: a reassuring healthy-senior image and pass-style wording (GOOD BALANCE, STRONG LEGS) hint at a quick balance check, but the test itself is not depicted.
composition: A vertical portrait with the face roughly centred in the strip and the caption box directly under the chin across the upper chest as a secondary focal point; the side bars are filler. Negative space is limited to a blurred bokeh background.
typography: Four words in white and green bold caps with two emojis inside a dark rounded box; the box spans about 69% of the centre strip (about 22% of the full frame width), so the small type is unreadable at 160x90. The caption states the result of the test, not the 10-second test from the title.
colors: Natural muted greens, grey shirt and warm skin tones; the two green words and check emoji are the only highlights. Mean contrast is low (soft photo) and no warning colour is used.
psychology: A warm toothy smile, relaxed posture and green check marks signal health, confidence and reassurance; no urgency or fear, which matches a "pass" implication.
partnership: Title says doctors recommend this 10-second test; the thumbnail shows a smiling man with "GOOD BALANCE STRONG LEGS", implying the outcome of the test but not the test or the doctor; the title's credential claim has no visual support.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the smiling face catches first in the upper strip, the dark caption box with green words second, and the blurred side bars are ignored.
art: Natural-looking photo with soft bokeh and plausible lighting; no visible compositing artefacts. The strip is a vertical shorts frame with blurred green extension, and the caption box covers the torso.
strength: A warm, genuine-looking photo and green check emoji create a positive, trustworthy mood.
weakness: The caption is tiny and the photo is generic stock-like, so the "10 second test" is never visualised.
bottleneck: Nothing shows what the test is, so the curiosity of the title is not carried by the picture.
action: Hypothesis: show the person doing the test (for example standing on one leg with a "10s" timer) in place of the portrait and test whether the action clarifies the premise.
counterexample: Seq 11 (THB-ad13c792db3d) is the opposite in text weight: a very dense, loud health layout rather than a small caption on a quiet photo.
